0.0.n: さん makes this way of addressing the audience polite and friendly.

0.1.n: This standard daytime greeting ends with は, pronounced わ.

1.0.n: Sets the occasion for the recording she is introducing.

1.2.n: This is the name of the game whose theme song she sang.

1.4.n: This English loanword identifies the song’s role.

1.6.n: An old-fashioned form of 忘れる with じ expressing a resolve not to forget, used in the song title.

1.7.n: Links 忘れじ to 言の葉 within the poetic song title.

1.8.n: A poetic expression for words or language, literally combining speech and leaves.

1.10.n: Marks the song title as what she sang.

1.11.n: 歌う becomes 歌わせて, followed by humble いただきました, politely presenting the performance as an opportunity she received.

2.0.n: This is her family name, placed before her given name.

2.1.n: This character begins the given name 希和子; the subtitle splits a single name here.

2.2.n: These characters complete 希和子, her given name; they are not a separate name here.

2.3.n: Politely completes her introduction; Japanese leaves out I here.

3.0.n: Identifies the area of work the speaker and his group are responsible for.

3.1.n: Connects 音楽 to the group name, indicating their musical role in this introduction.

3.2.n: This begins the group name 未来古代楽団 and literally means future.

3.3.n: This is the middle part of the group name 未来古代楽団.

3.4.n: This completes the group name 未来古代楽団.

3.6.n: This character begins the family name 砂守; the subtitle splits the name unnaturally.

3.7.n: This chunk crosses a name boundary: 守 completes 砂守, while 岳 begins the given name 岳央.

3.8.n: This character completes 岳央, his given name; it is not a separate word here.

3.9.n: Politely ends his self-introduction after his full name.

4.0.n: Shows that she shares the previous speaker’s group affiliation and musical role.

4.1.n: This is her family name, which comes before her given name.

4.2.n: This is her given name; Japanese names can have readings that are difficult to predict.

4.3.n: Makes the introduction polite without needing an explicit I.

0.tip: 皆さん is a friendly, polite way to address a whole audience.

1.lit: This time, Grimms Notes theme song Words of Never Forgetting, I was allowed to sing.
1.tip: 歌わせていただきました humbly presents singing as an opportunity received, rather than simply saying I sang.

2.tip: The full name is 安次嶺 希和子; do not treat 希 and 和子 as separate names.

3.lit: For music, Mirai Kodai Gakudan, Sunamori Taketeru am.
3.tip: The speaker’s name divides as 砂守 岳央, not according to the displayed word chunks.

4.tip: 同じく avoids repeating the group affiliation just given by the previous speaker.
